text:
amy.sales: Quick sync — AcmeBank final-mile asks before we sign POC SOW. High level: BYO-HSM (they insist), perf/latency impact, rotation automation, security questionnaire Qs (attestation, split custody), and pen-test scheduling. Can we confirm any hard blockers and a recommended runbook for the POC cutover?

omar.engineering: We support BYO-HSM via our HSM-proxy. Tenant isolation: each customer runs an isolated proxy VM + mTLS to the HSM. Network: we need their HSM's public egress CIDRs/ports (usually 443). Perf: expect ~5–20ms added per request depending on key ops and regional hops.

lucy.security: From security's POV we need: A) HSM attestation report (cert chain) B) key export disabled proof C) FIPS level or equivalent D) key custody model. If they want split custody (dual-custodian) that's not native for our hosted HSM; we can propose compensating controls (audit logs to their SIEM, restricted operator roles, attestations).

patrik.sre: For the POC cutover we recommend a rolling key swap with 5-minute overlap and a 2-hour maintenance window in case of failures. We'll run a dry-run first in staging. Also need the customer's expected TPS and percent of requests that will do KEK unwraps vs cached prefixes.

jen.solutions: Pricing note: BYO-HSM proxy overhead = approx +20% on token cost for POC sizing. If they commit to Dedicated reserved capacity we can offer a discount; need confirmed QPS and token/sec numbers to firm up.

amy.sales: They asked specifically: can we automate monthly rotation (customer-managed rotation triggered by their KMS) and still keep continuous availability? Also pen-test: they want to run a pen test against the proxy and control-plane within the POC window — is that allowed?

omar.engineering: Yes for rotation: we support API-driven rotation. Typical flow: 1) create new wrapping key 2) stage key for 5m overlap 3) switch routing to new key 4) deprecate old key. We can expose endpoints for that. For pen tests: allowed with prior coordination; must sign the pentest agreement and schedule with SRE.

lucy.security: Pen test policy: sign NDA + pentest window request form. We require at least 5 business days notice and a scoped test plan. We cannot permit destructive actions against production nodes; will provide a staging environment.

patrik.sre: Add on network: they must whitelist our staging proxy IPs. For live POC we'll need a maintenance window and a rollback playbook. I'll own the runbook.

jen.solutions: I'll update the SOW: include BYO-HSM addendum, +20% POC premium, and explicit pen-test approval clause (NDA + 5 days notice). Also add acceptance criteria: key attestation proof AND successful dry-run rotation in staging.

amy.sales: Excellent. Customer also has Q12 on the security questionnaire: "Can Redwood support multi-custodian key ceremonies?" What's the shortest, customer-friendly answer we can give?

lucy.security: Short answer: we don't provide multi-custodian HSM workflows out-of-the-box. We can offer: 1) documented key ceremony procedure run with their ops team (we can be present) 2) attestation snapshots and audit logs 3) if required, a professional services engagement to implement split-control using their HSM solution.

omar.engineering: For engineering handoff to customer, I'll prepare a minimal integration checklist and a sample config. Share a quick snippet they can use to test connectivity to the HSM-proxy: 
```bash
# test TLS connection to our proxy (replace HOST)
curl -v https://hsm-proxy.acme-test.redwood.ai/health --cacert /path/to/attestation_ca.pem
```

jen.solutions: I'll attach the cost delta sheet and draft SOW to the deal in doc (link: https://redwood.app/sales/doc/ACME-POC-BYOHSM).

amy.sales: Perfect. Action items: jen — update SOW and pricing, include acceptance criteria; lucy — draft the short answer + compensating controls for Q12; omar — checklist + sample snippets + perf note; patrik — runbook + pret-test scheduling window. I'll send the next update to the customer by EOD. :thumbsup:

redwood-bot: Document uploaded: ACME_POC_BYOHSM_Attestation_Checklist.pdf

amy.sales: Thanks all — ping me here if you hit any blockers.
